# DRLG cathedral + catacombs + caves + hell + Hellfire crypt + dPiece goldens (devilGo-76tu, devilGo-4ybb)

Committed, Go-owned parity fixtures for the four DRLG generators ported so far:
`CreateL5Dungeon` (`drlg_l1.cpp:1299-1345`) on the two level types it serves —
`DTYPE_CATHEDRAL` (level 1) and `DTYPE_CRYPT` (Hellfire levels 21-24) —
`CreateL2Dungeon` (`drlg_l2.cpp:2830-2837`) on `DTYPE_CATACOMBS` (levels 5-8),
`CreateL3Dungeon` (`drlg_l3.cpp:2185-2193`) on `DTYPE_CAVES` (levels 9-12) and
`CreateL4Dungeon` (`drlg_l4.cpp:1228-1236`) on `DTYPE_HELL` (levels 13-16).
All are dispatched by `CreateDungeon` (`gendung.cpp:346-370`), whose
`GetLevelType` (`gendung.cpp:326-344`) picks the generator from the level
number.

Tests read only these files. They never read MPQs, the devilutionX tree, or the
network; a missing or malformed fixture fails the test.

## Corpus

`l<level>-<entry>-<seed>.csv`, 40 variants × 8 pinned seeds = 320 files:

| level | leveltype | source |
|---|---|---|
| 1-4 | `DTYPE_CATHEDRAL` (1) | `drlg_l1.cpp` cathedral branch |
| 5-8 | `DTYPE_CATACOMBS` (2) | `drlg_l2.cpp` `CreateL2Dungeon` |
| 9-12 | `DTYPE_CAVES` (3) | `drlg_l3.cpp` `CreateL3Dungeon` |
| 13-16 | `DTYPE_HELL` (4) | `drlg_l4.cpp` `CreateL4Dungeon` |
| 21-24 | `DTYPE_CRYPT` (6) | `crypt.cpp` variant |

Levels 2-4 are included because they are the cathedral levels (`CreateL5Dungeon`
serves all of `DTYPE_CATHEDRAL`): 2 exercises the Butcher set piece, 3 the
Skeleton King set piece, 4 the banner set piece plus the Poisoned Water Supply
entrance and its stairs rule.

Levels 5-8 are the catacombs levels (`CreateL2Dungeon` serves all of
`DTYPE_CATACOMBS`): each runs the same generator with the level's own quest
state (`DRLG_CheckQuests`, `drlg_l2.cpp:2818`), which is why all four are
pinned rather than level 5 alone.

Levels 9-12 are the caves levels (`CreateL3Dungeon` serves all of
`DTYPE_CAVES`): level 9 adds the town-warp miniset (`drlg_l3.cpp:1945`) and
reserves the anvil room while `Q_ANVIL` is available
(`drlg_l3.cpp:2005-2011,2022`), so the four levels are not layout-equivalent
and all four are pinned.

Levels 13-16 are the hell levels (`CreateL4Dungeon` serves all of `DTYPE_HELL`):
15 is the Diablo/pentagram level (`drlg_l4.cpp:1201`) and 16 runs the
`ProtectQuads`/`LoadDiabQuads` path (`drlg_l4.cpp:1166-1168,1180-1182`), which
is why the whole range is pinned.

Each CSV holds four records (the format `internal/diablo/testsupport.EncodeDunCSV`
writes): the two tile-layer dimensions, the row-major 40×40 `dungeon` tile ids,
the row-major 80×80 `dTransVal` window (rows 16..95, columns 16..95 of the
112×112 array), and `ViewX,ViewY,leveltype`.

## dPiece/dSpecial corpus (Pass3)

`dpiece/l<level>-dpiece-<entry>-<seed>.csv`, 32 variants × 8 pinned seeds = 256
files (the 320 tile-layer files plus `manifest.txt` stay untouched). They live
in their own `dpiece/` subdirectory because the tile-layer parity tests glob
`l*-*.csv` in this directory and every such file must hold the four-record
tile-layer shape. These pin the next DRLG unit:
the Pass3 expansion every generator runs at its end — `DRLG_LPass3`
(`gendung.cpp:591`) turns the 40×40 tile layer into the 112×112 `dPiece`
mega-tile grid by looking each tile up in the level's `lN.til`, and
`drlg_l1.cpp:402` / `drlg_l2.cpp:1663` `InitDungeonPieces` read that grid back
to write `dSpecial` (the door/arch markers).

Format, same record style as the tile-layer CSVs:

| record | content |
|---|---|
| 1 | `112,112` — `MAXDUNX,MAXDUNY` |
| 2 | `dPiece` — 12544 uint16 values |
| 3 | `dSpecial` — 12544 int8 values, **present only when the grid has a non-zero cell** |

Both grids are x-major like the probe artifacts (cell `(x, y)` at
`x*112+y`, `dun_tile_data.hpp:99,136`). Records 1-2 always appear; cathedral
(1-4) and catacombs (5-8) add record 3, caves and hell leave `dSpecial` zero at
generation time and carry no third record.

Unlike the tile-layer goldens, this corpus needs the level's real mega-tile
table: `DRLG_LPass3` expands whatever `pMegaTiles` holds, so the probe installs
`lN.til` through `LoadLvlGFX` (`diablo.cpp:1360`, via the additive
`ProbeLoadLvlGFX`/`ProbeFreeLvlGFX` shims in the probe patch) before each
variant. `dPiece` values therefore depend on `DIABDAT.MPQ` level data, which is
why these files are committed rather than regenerated by the tests.

## Set-piece data

`setpieces/<name>.csv` is the dimension header plus the tile layer of the `.dun`
files the generator loads by name (`drlg_l1.cpp:386-394`, `crypt.cpp:690,701`):
`rnd6`/`skngdo`/`banner2` from `DIABDAT.MPQ levels/l1data`, `blind1`/`blood1`/
`blood2`/`bonestr1`/`bonestr2` from `DIABDAT.MPQ levels/l2data`,
`cornerstone`/`uberroom` from devilutionX `mods/hf` (`assets/hf/nlevels/l5data`).

## Producer

Offline, once, against the pinned commit `ca91d778f`:

1. `git -C devilutionX worktree add /tmp/dvlx-pinned ca91d778f`
2. add `add_subdirectory(${DVG_PROBE_DIR} dvg-probe)` to `CMake/Tests.cmake`,
   configure with `-DBUILD_TESTING=ON -DDVG_PROBE_DIR=<repo>/tools/probe`, build
   the `dvg_probe` target, copy `DIABDAT.MPQ`, `hellfire.mpq` and
   `devilutionx.mpq` next to it.
3. `dvg_probe drlg <out> tools/probe/seeds.txt` — one `.dun` + `.meta` per
   variant and seed, dumped **before** `CreateThemeRooms()` (theme rooms are
   devilGo-foug's scope, so these goldens pin only the generator).
   `dvg_probe stages <out> tools/probe/seeds.txt` additionally writes the
   per-attempt caves/hell stage layers (`<stage>-<level>-<state>.bin`) against
   the `l3l4stages` patch; those dumps are diagnostics for the port and are
   not committed.
4. `go run ./tools/probe/dunconv <out>/drlg internal/testdata/drlg` converts
   every pair to CSV (dims, tiles, transparency window, view position,
   leveltype) through `testsupport.EncodeDunCSV`, the same encoder the tests
   read the corpus back with. `manifest.txt` carries the sha256 of every
   committed file.
5. dPiece corpus: `dvg_probe dpiece <out> tools/probe/seeds.txt` writes one
   `.bin` per level/entry/seed (levels 1-16), and
   `go run ./tools/probe/dunconv dpiece <out>/dpiece internal/testdata/drlg/dpiece`
   converts them to the `dpiece/l*-dpiece-*.csv` goldens.

Both artifact layers are **x-major**: the probe copies
`dungeon[MAXDUNX][MAXDUNY]` and `dTransVal[MAXDUNX][MAXDUNY]`
(`Source/levels/dun_tile_data.cpp:52-53`) linearly, so cell (x, y) sits at
`x*height+y`; `ParseDunArtifact` exposes that as `[y][x]` and `EncodeDunCSV`
flattens it back to the artifact order.

The same build reproduces all 256 committed `dun/` artifacts byte-identically
(manifest sha256 check), which is the provenance check for the producer.

Each `drlg/` fixture is a pure function of (level, seed): two independent
`dvg_probe drlg` runs, plus a run with the level order reversed, produce a
byte-identical corpus (`diff -r` over the 320 CSVs, 2026-11-04).

## Set-piece format (fixed 2026-11-04)

A set-piece CSV holds the `.dun` tile layer as **uint16 tile values**, one
decimal per cell, after a `width,height` first record. `encodeDun` in
`l1_parity_test.go` rebuilds the file as `uint16 w, uint16 h, w*h uint16 LE`,
which is what `GetDunSize`/`PlaceDunTiles` read.

The five CSVs first committed with this corpus were wrong: they held the raw
**byte** stream of the tile layer, so every value looked like `4,0,7,0,...` and
`encodeDun` rebuilt a layer whose tiles were `4,0,7,0,...` instead of
`4,7,7,4,...` — a set piece the C++ generator never placed. The goldens in this
directory are unaffected (they come from the real `.dun` inside the C++ run),
so the defect only showed up as a cathedral parity mismatch on the levels that
use a set piece (2, 3, 4).

All six CSVs are now regenerated from the pinned assets and verified to
round-trip: `encodeDun` output equals the first `4+2*w*h` bytes of the real
`.dun` byte for byte (`cornerstone`, `uberroom` checked explicitly;
`rnd6`/`skngdo`/`banner2`/`banner1` read from `DIABDAT.MPQ` with the ported Go
MPQ reader).

`banner1` (`levels/l1data/banner1.dun`) is added because
`DRLG_CheckQuests`→`DrawLTBanner` (levels/drlg_quests.cpp:56-80) loads it on
level 4. It writes `pdungeon`, not `dungeon`, so it does not change the tile
goldens.

## Mega-tile tables (Pass3)

`assets/l<family>.{til,min}.csv` hold the two archive members a level installs
before it is generated:

- `levels/lNdata/lN.til` is `pMegaTiles` — four `uint16` micro tiles per mega
tile (`levels/dun_tile_data.hpp:56-61`), the table `DRLG_LPass3`
(`levels/gendung.cpp:585-621`) expands into `dPiece`. `LoadLvlGFX` reads it
(`levels/diablo.cpp:1360-1400`).
- `levels/lNdata/lN.min` is the per-piece CEL block table `LoadMinData`
(`levels/dun_tile_data.cpp:69-93`) feeds to `SetDungeonMicros`
(`levels/dun_tile_data.cpp:167-205`), which builds `DPieceMicros`/`SOLData` for
the renderer. The generator does not read it; it is committed so the render
side of the same pieces has the same offline source.

Both are text CSVs, not raw binaries
(repo decision: binary dumps are committed as text), and `assets/manifest.txt`
carries the sha256 of the raw archive member each CSV re-encodes to byte for
byte: `uint16 LE count, uint16 LE cols, count*cols uint16 LE values`, `cols=4`
for `.til` and `cols=1` for `.min`.

The Hellfire hive tables (`nlevels/l6data/l6.{til,min,sol}`) are committed
with the hive goldens (see Hive below). The crypt's `nlevels/l5data` set is not
extracted yet: the crypt dPiece gate owns that fixture.

## Town (devilGo-t1lp)

`town/l0-town-main-<seed>.csv`, 8 seeds from `tools/probe/seeds.txt`:
`CreateTown` (`town.cpp:359-387`) serves `DTYPE_TOWN` only, takes no seed, and
its layout is four fixed `.dun` files, so the corpus is one entry and eight
seeds instead of the 40 variants the procedural generators need. The full
surface map is `docs/research/dg-town-inventory.md`.

Each file holds five records:

| # | Record | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `112,112` | world-tile dims (`MAXDUNX`,`MAXDUNY`) |
| 2 | 12544 values | `dPiece`, x-major (`x*MAXDUNY+y`) |
| 3 | 12544 values | `dSpecial`, x-major (`InitTownPieces`, `town.cpp:149-186`) |
| 4 | `40,40` | tile-layer dims (`DMAXX`,`DMAXY`) |
| 5 | 1600 values | `dungeon`, the automap tile layer + closed-warp patches |

Records 1-3 keep the dPiece-corpus shape, so the same parser reads both; record
5 is separate because town pins both the mega-tile expansion (`FillSector`) and
the tile layer `automap.dun` + the `dungeon[x][y]` patches write.

`ENTRY_MAIN` and `ENTRY_PREV` produce a byte-identical layout — the entry only
moves `ViewPosition` (`town.cpp:364-384`) — so the probe compares the two at dump
time and fails rather than writing a second identical file.

`dTransVal` is dumped but never committed: `DRLG_InitTrans` (`gendung.cpp:384-389`)
zeroes it and no town path writes it. `tools/probe/dunconv` fails the conversion if any
cell is non-zero, so the omission is checked, not assumed.

Seeds matter: the ten `PickRandomlyAmong({1,2,3,4})` draws in the closed
hell-warp branch (`town.cpp:220-227`) are the only RNG consumer, and the probe
pins `SetRndSeed(seed)` because upstream does not pin it here. All eight dumps
are distinct.

`assets/town.til.csv` is this level's `pMegaTiles` (`nlevels/towndata/town.til`,
376 mega tiles). Probe state: single player, no hellfire quest progress, fresh
hero — so catacombs/caves/hell warps are all closed and the hellfire hive/grave
patches are skipped.

### Town `.dun` inputs (`town/inputs/`)

`CreateTown` loads five fixed `.dun` files by path (`town.cpp:202-207`). The
parity test never reads an MPQ, so each one is committed as a tile-layer CSV in
the set piece format: `width,height` then `width*height` uint16 tile ids.

| Fixture | Upstream path | Source archive | Dims |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sector1s.csv` | `levels\towndata\sector1s.dun` | `DIABDAT.MPQ` | 25×25 |
| `sector2s.csv` | `levels\towndata\sector2s.dun` | `DIABDAT.MPQ` | 25×23 |
| `sector3s.csv` | `levels\towndata\sector3s.dun` | `DIABDAT.MPQ` | 23×25 |
| `sector4s.csv` | `levels\towndata\sector4s.dun` | `DIABDAT.MPQ` | 23×23 |
| `automap.csv` | `levels\towndata\automap.dun` | `devilutionx.mpq` | 40×40 |

The four sectors tile the 96×96 piece grid exactly (23+23 = 46, 25+25 = 50 on
the piece halves); `automap.dun` is the `dungeon` tile layer the pass patches.
Regenerate from an offline asset extraction:

```sh
go run ./tools/probe/dunconv town-inputs <raw-dun-dir> internal/testdata/drlg/town
```

`<raw-dun-dir>` holds the five files under their base name. The encoder is
`testsupport.EncodeDunTilesCSV` and the decoder `testsupport.DecodeDunTilesCSV`
rebuilds the `.dun` prefix (two LE dimensions plus the LE uint16 tile layer) the
loader reads, so a refresh and the test share one codec
(`testsupport/dun_tiles_test.go` round-trips every committed fixture).

## Hive / nest (levels 17-20, devilGo-kmme)

`dpiece/l1{7,8,9}-dpiece-<entry>-<seed>.csv` and `l20` — 4 levels × 2 entries ×
8 seeds = 64 files, the `dpiece` shape above (two records; the hive writes no
`dSpecial`, like caves). `DTYPE_NEST` (`gendung.cpp:335`) routes to
`CreateL3Dungeon` with the nest branches in `drlg_l3.cpp` (pool `:1499-1501`,
stairs `:1982-1989`, isles `:2034-2042`) and to the unconditional
`DRLG_LPass3(8 - 1)` at `:2149-2152`, so the same expansion runs on the hive's
own `nlevels/l6data/l6.til` (166 mega tiles, `LoadLvlGFX` `diablo.cpp:1409-1413`).

**These goldens are targets, not a pass gate yet:** the Go hive generator does
not exist. `hive_parity_test.go` drives the planned `GenerateNest` seam and is
RED (`errNotImplemented`) until the port lands; the fixtures exist so the port
starts against a fixed target, exactly as the town CSVs did.

`assets/l6.{til,min,sol}.csv` are the three `nlevels/l6data` members the nest
branch installs, encoded with the `.til`/`.min` codec above (`.sol` re-encodes
as one byte per value, 606 bytes — below `MAXTILES`). Producer additions, both
dump-only: `dvg_probe` gained the nest variants in `DpieceVariants` and loads
`hellfire.mpq` for them (`LoadHellfireArchives`, `engine/assets.cpp:570` — the
nest graphics are not in the mod-only archive set), and `dunconv assets <mpq>
<dir>` encodes the members. The same probe run reproduces all 256 committed
dPiece CSVs for levels 1-16 byte-identically, which is the provenance check.
